HCBCOGN312.contribution: Directly teaches language acquisition, bilingualism, speech, semantics and experimental approaches, with a neuroscience emphasis.
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

MCCHEAM316.contribution: Historiography and interpretive methods develop critical reading of disciplinary scholarship about art.
MCCHEAM316.topics: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Through critical readings of influential texts by figures such as Aby Warburg, Erwin Panofsky, Ernst Gombrich, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida, students explore the major ideas and methodologies that have shaped the field. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.

candidateAssessment.concept: Dutch Language, Literary Interpretation and Rhetoric
candidateAssessment.assessment: Dutch supplies introductory pronunciation, grammar and cultural comparison. Style & Meaning teaches linguistic and stylistic analysis, while Psycholinguistics directly examines acquisition, bilingualism and comprehension experimentally. Literary analysis, world texts, creative writing and rhetoric offer meaningful disciplinary methods. These methods are not developed through Dutch literary texts across periods, historical Dutch or a sustained analysis of contemporary Dutch usage.

Psycholinguistics directly studies bilingualism and acquisition. Stylistics, higher cognition, introductory Dutch and sociology support language and identity inquiry. Native American Histories examines Indigenous storytelling, assimilation and cultural continuity in a distinct setting. Text methods and media contribute complementary tools. The trial does not develop Frisian language preservation, historical linguistics or literary inquiry as a sustained subject.

World myth, literary meaning, life writing, art, film and creative writing supply comparative interpretation across genres and cultural contexts. Introductory Dutch adds basic grammar and everyday cultural practices. The texts and cultural cases do not form a Dutch literary history, and the concept has little sustained linguistics.

academicFinding: UCR offers introductory Dutch, psycholinguistics, literary interpretation, rhetoric and creative writing. These courses develop useful language and literary skills. The feasible combinations do not provide sustained study of Dutch-language literature across periods or of the historical development, structure and use of Dutch. Those subjects organise the selected Groningen track and its research training. The separate Frisian direction also requires sustained study of its language, literature and regional culture.
